text:
I am Dominga Villalba;
I was born in the furrow
where my mother sowed.

The hammock that served as my cradle
was braided by absence
and hung by oblivion.
Pablo, they say, was his name.
He never came to see me!

The road of the poor
is found always
only by pain.

Papers, sealed with injustice.
Rifles, loaded with ignominy.

Shack, fields, hopes, everything!
was someone else’s.
Ours,
only a little
of calloused flesh
and a great love fed
by earth, dew,
birds and ears of grain.

Now I am Dominga Villalba,
a worker,
rebellious and combative,
voice and fist in the struggle
for bread and land.
That is how they made me!
With blows they worked
my country clay
and now I am
steel fiber!

translation.title: The Little Working Girl
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The class struggle and transformation remain intact.
